'''Hugh Felkin''' (1922–2001)<ref name="AC">{{cite web |title=Hugh Felkin nous a quittés le 9 novembre 2001 - p44 - N°253 - L'Actualité Chimique, le journal de la SCF |url=https://new.societechimiquedefrance.fr/numero/hugh-felkin-nous-a-quittes-le-9-novembre-2001-p44-n253/?lang=en |website=Société Chimique de France (SCF) |access-date=31 December 2021}}</ref> was a research [[chemist]] in [[France]] from 1950 to 1990 and a member of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].

In 1967, he proposed a model to predict the [[stereochemistry|stereochemical]] outcome of the addition of [[nucleophile]]s to [[Carbonyl|carbonylic compounds]]. This model (now known as the [[Asymmetric induction|Felkin-Anh model]])<ref name="AC"/> differs slightly from [[Cram's rule of asymmetric induction|Cram's rule]] and it is one of the most accepted rules to predict the outcome of these reactions.

He finished his career as [[Directeur de recherche|Directeur de Recherche]] at the [[Institut de Chimie des Substances Naturelles]] in Gif-sur-Yvette.<ref name="AC"/> His laboratory worked on organometallic chemistry, with a special focus on organorhenium chemistry.

Born in England on 18 January 1922, he spent the second world war years in [[Geneva]] studying chemistry.<ref name="AC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.unige.ch/archives/files/7515/4028/4985/Diplomes_1945-1946.pdf |title="Grades, diplômes et certificats décernés par l'Université de Genève pendant l'année 1945-46"|access-date=31 December 2021}}</ref> At that time the requirements for a degree were "to show sufficient knowledge in chemistry".

After completing his studies, he went to France to work for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]]. In France he met Irène, born Elphimoff, also a research chemist, who became his wife and survived him by 9 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Espace de Recueillement de Madame Irene ELPHIMOFF |url=https://www.libramemoria.com/defunts/elphimoff-irene/8dc368a0c58d4086915ebda742417c90 |website=www.libramemoria.com |access-date=30 December 2021 |language=FR-fr}}</ref> They had one daughter, Mary, born in 1962.

He was a member of the communist party until the communist coup in Prague in 1948. After this disappointment, his sympathies still firmly inclined towards the left, he read ''[[Le Monde]]'' without which he used to say he didn't know what to think.  Other sayings for which he was noted were "Je suis anti-sioniste mais je n'arrive pas à être pro-arabe", and in case of any uncertainty on the part of the presenter in group meetings, "il ne s'agit pas de croire, il s'agit de savoir".

Distinguished alumni of Hugh's lab include [[:fr:Bernard Meunier|Bernard Meunier]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Bernard Meunier - Bandeau - CNRS |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww2.cnrs.fr%2Fband%2F367.htm#federation=archive.wikiwix.com |website=archive.wikiwix.com |access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref> (president of the CNRS 2004-2006), [[Stephen G. Davies|Steve Davies]]<ref>{{cite web | url = http://davies.chem.ox.ac.uk/group_steve.html | title = About Steve Davies | access-date = 2012-06-24 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100531191156/http://davies.chem.ox.ac.uk/group_steve.html | archive-date = 2010-05-31 }}</ref> creator of major spinouts at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Oxford Asymmetry agrees to German merger worth £316m |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/news/oxford-asymmetry-agrees-to-german-merger-worth-pound-316m-711974.html |access-date=30 December 2021 |publisher=The Independent |date=31 July 2000 |language=en}}</ref> and [[Robert H. Crabtree|Bob Crabtree]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Crabtree Gives Prestigious Franco-American Chemistry Prize Lecture {{!}} Department of Chemistry |url=https://chem.yale.edu/news/crabtree-gives-prestigious-franco-american-chemistry-prize-lecture |website=chem.yale.edu |access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref>
